newsitem.title: THAILAND: Italian-Thai in Burma hydro dam study.
newsitem.headline: Italian-Thai in Burma hydro dam study.

text.p: Thai construction firm Italian-Thai Development Plc (ITD) said on Wednesday it and a consortium had signed an agreement to do a feasibility study for developing a hydro dam in Burma.
Under the agreement, the consortium, which consists of Italian-Thai, Marubeni and MDX Plc, will conduct a 15-month feasibility study on developing the dam, ITD said in a statement.
The dam is expected to be situated on the Mae Kok river in Burma's northern Shan state, it added.
If the study shows that the project is feasible, the consortium will construct a reservoir, hydro dam and electricity supply system on the river, the company said.
The project cost would be about 6.0 billion baht (US$240 million) the dam will be completed in 2002, it said.
The three companies will also set up a joint venture with an initial capital of 25 million baht for operating the project.
Italian-Thai and Marubeni will hold 35 percent stake each in the joint venture, while MDX will hold the rest.
